title: House Rules Plugin Audit
eyebrow: Audit of house-rules 2.68.0 before a restructure · findings, diagrams and recommendations · nothing built yet

short.lead: I read the whole plugin: its rules, docs, hook.py, the test suite and the smaller scripts. It works, and all 832 checks pass, but it no longer agrees with itself. Rules contradict rules in 28 places, docs contradict code in 20, and code contradicts its own logic in 15. It also can't work for anyone but you, because 62 lines in 15 shipped files hard-code your name, your repos or your labels. Most of this comes from one 8,365-line file doing every job, with each rule copied into several places. Claude Code now provides four features that the plugin built for itself, so the restructure can use those instead.
short.hint: Tap a card to see the evidence behind it.
items: One file, 30 hook commands, state in five places

scripts/hook.py holds 8,365 lines and 284 functions. It answers 9 Claude Code events (moments such as session start or the end of a reply) through 30 entry points, meaning separate commands the events can trigger, and it has 35 on/off switches. State is spread over the temp folder, .git, the repo's .claude/ folder, ~/.claude and GitHub. verify.py is one 9,747-line script, and each of its checks launches hook.py as a separate program run.

items.alt: Diagram: nine hook events feed thirty entry points in one hook.py file, which writes state to five different places
items.caption: Today's structure

items: The plugin breaks its own rules

Autosave commits credit Claude and sign as house-rules@localhost (hook.py:4896-4915), which the guard refuses on every other commit. When Python is missing, 20 of the 30 entry points exit without saying anything (run.sh:106-156), which breaks the rule "Nothing fails silently". Five end-of-reply checks look only at the newest message, so today a shorter retry slipped past the page check.

items.alt: Bar chart: 28 rule contradictions, 20 doc-code, 15 code-logic, 8 doc-doc, 3 script, 10 stale citations, 9 duplicates, 20 silent entry points, 62 personal lines
items.caption: Findings counted by kind

items: Claude Code now does four of these jobs

Plugin dependencies: one plugin can require another, so a sub-plugin can require a shared core. userConfig: a settings list each user fills in once, with their own name, credit line and labels. autoUpdate: a marketplace setting that fetches new plugin versions by itself, plus the /reload-plugins command to load them in a running session. And a data folder for each plugin, whose location is held in CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA. A guide helper checked all four against the official plugin docs today.

changes: new
A shared core plugin
Hook runner, one config, one state store, rules from one source each.

Every sub-plugin lists the core as a dependency in its plugin.json, so installing any one of them installs the core too. Identity (name, credit line, labels, owner, branch prefix) comes from userConfig, the settings each user fills in, instead of being written into the code. Every failure says so, including a missing Python.
Everything lives in one plugin, and your identity is written directly into the code in 62 lines.
A core that holds only what every part needs, configured per user.
Anyone can install it, and each user sets their own values once with /plugin configure.

changes.alt: Diagram: five optional sub-plugins (Safe git, Design loop, Writing, Delegation, Docs) sit on one shared core
changes.caption: Proposed structure

changes: new
Five optional sub-plugins
Safe git, Design loop, Writing, Delegation and Docs, each installable on its own.

Safe git: the destructive and branch guard, the overwrite guard, credit checks and the prompt timer. Design loop: stages, approvals, issues, pages, QA and the end-of-reply checks. Writing: one clarity checker, the editor helper and plain docs. Delegation: helper agents, the limit on how many run at once, audits and worktree autosave. Docs: the doc tiers, the long-comment harvest, doc-ref pointers and the archivist helper that moves long comments into docs.
One plugin, all or nothing.
Each part installs on its own and registers its own end-of-reply checks.
Someone who wants just the git protections installs nothing else.
chg
Rule text
One source file per rule, and 28 contradictions settled.
Each rule exists as a summary and a detail file, plus copies in the output style, the agent files, the docs and the code's messages.
One file per rule, from which the injected text and the docs are generated.

The grilling session decides each contradiction first. Two examples: one rule allows deletes because git can restore them, and another refuses deletes for that same reason. One rule says to run test suites twice, and another says to run them exactly once.
chg
End-of-reply checks (event_handover)
Every check judges the whole turn, meaning all replies since your last message.
The card, plain-summary, writing, long-reply and choices checks read only the newest message.
Each check reads every reply since your last message, so a short retry can't clear a block.
Two page-saved checklist entries that never run are removed (hook.py:7485, 7519-7520).
chg
Writing checks
One checker everywhere, aware of definitions and quotes.
clarity.py and plain_docs_check.py treat text in backticks differently, and neither notices when a term is defined in the text or quoted.
One checker; a term defined in the same text, or quoted while reporting a flag, isn't flagged.
This is why one technical word was flagged three times in a row today, even after a reply explained it.

Replaced: verify.py
Small tests for each module, plus a few full runs for each hook event.
One 9,747-line script with 832 checks, every one launching hook.py as a separate program run, and 214 lines checking that copies of the same text have not drifted apart.
Small tests for the logic in each module, a few full runs per event, and no copy-matching tests once each rule has a single source.
The test count becomes a result, not a goal.

Replaced: version check and self-update
Marketplace autoUpdate and /reload-plugins.
The event_versioncheck function fetches the latest version from GitHub, runs claude plugin update, and prints a notice, which today wrongly said the old version was still running.
Claude Code's own autoUpdate setting, which updates the plugin by itself. The notice only says that a newer version is installed and that /reload-plugins loads it.
hook.py:1471-1633 goes.

Dropped: account-wide re-inject marker
The build plan from earlier today stops here, and this marker is not built.
A git ref (a named pointer inside your repo) recording, once per account, that the new rules were loaded again after an update.
Nothing replaces it. Another person's install has no shared place to keep it, and /reload-plugins already handles each session.
The fix to the version notice becomes part of the shared core instead.

Dropped: the old step-card template
templates/step-card.html.
A second page template, with a hard-coded C:\Users\aj path in it.
Only make_page.py and handover-page.html.
It contradicts the rule that every page comes from the page builder.
keep
Guards, prompt timer, page builder, harvest, helpers, profile, standards
They work; each moves into its sub-plugin.

Four small fixes ride along with the restructure. The destructive and branch guard refuses a tool call that arrives with no tool input, instead of letting it through. The overwrite guard's docstring is corrected to say it refuses, which is what it does. The builder helper (agents/builder.md) is changed to run the full test suites twice, as rules/detail/green-suite.md says, instead of once. The archivist helper gets a line listing the tools it may use.
choices: What is the plugin's core identity, and so its default install?
Guardrails: the core plus Safe git, with the other four optional
The guards protect any user's work on day one, and they need the least configuration.
A design-first workflow: the core plus Design loop as the default
The most distinctive part, but it changes how every session runs, and a new user may not want that.
Stay one plugin, split into modules inside it
Smallest move, but users still get everything or nothing.
My recommendation is Guardrails, the core plus Safe git: every user benefits from it without changing how they work.

wrapup.summary: Split the plugin into a shared core and five optional sub-plugins, move identity into per-user settings, use Claude Code's built-ins for updates, state and dependencies, and settle the 28 rule contradictions before building.
wrapup.changing: Nothing yet. This page proposes a direction. The full findings, each with file:line on both sides, are in docs/audits/2026-10-16-plugin-audit/.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick for the core identity (Guardrails, a design-first workflow, or one plugin split into modules), and your approval of the direction.
